newsitem.title: UK: Benor forecasts $5 mln net profit for '97.
newsitem.headline: Benor forecasts $5 mln net profit for '97.

text.p: Oslo-listed shipping operator Benor Tankers Ltd forecast on Tuesday that a net profit of $5 million was possible in 1997.
Benor Tankers said the acquisition of five vessels earlier this year should lead to positive cash flow exceeding original projections of $30 million.

"Results from operations, despite this year being negatively influenced by the latest acquisitions, augmented by capital gains resulting from disposal of assets during July, should make a net profit of around $5 million a realistic target," Benor said.
The Bermuda-registered company reported that the second quarter of the year, traditionally not the most active period for the oil industry, had produced further improved results.
Benor said first half net profit in 1997 amounted to $1.4 million compared with $800,000 in the first six months of 1996.
Operating results of $11.5 million were $2.3 million higher than in the same period last year, the company said in a statement to the Oslo Bourse.
Positive cash flow, which after minority interests amounted to $8.1 million in the first quarter, reached $15.3 million for the first six months, it said.
Average net time charter equivalent rates per day reached $15,302, Benor said, an improvement of $140 over the first quarter and a five percent increase over the full year average of 1996.
Benor added that six month average all-in operating expenses per day were slightly below last year's figure at $5,411.
The ship acquisitions had necessitated further financing amounting to a total $20 million, equally distributed between shareholders Exmar and TransPetrol.
Financing was arranged through the issue of 1.36 million new shares at $8.50 per share and distribution of 995,348 shares held in treasury at the same price.
A seven year term loan of $68 million, granted by DnB Oslo, with participation of Deutsche Schiffsbank and Swedbank, was also used to finance the vessels.
ING Bank also granted a $46 million 10-year unsyndicated term loan, to fund new building in South Korea.
Following the recent acquisitions, Benor's total consolidated debt will represent about 55 percent of market value adjusted assets, it said.
After the redistribution of treasury stock and fleet expansion, Benor said its adjusted net asset value was estimated at more than $9.00 per share.
